quadruple.stage: Finite labelled subsets of integer pure-power supplies, using periodic binary-exponent blocks and elementary ordered subset-sum arithmetic.

shape.objects: Every input D is a finite rigid integer set with minimum four and bases eight and sixteen present; k and finite labelled deletion F vary without bound. Witnesses are finite subsets of pairs of natural numbers, with Finset, products, powers, finite sums and gcd available in Lean/Mathlib. Disjoint finite supports extend by union, and fresh unit alternatives can amplify an interval before adjoining a separate infinite reserve. Finite supports can be treated as random variables, but no spread condition is recorded.
shape.quantifiers: For every such finite D, every positive integer k and every finite labelled deletion F, there exists N(D,k,F), for every integer n>=N there is a finite subset of the remaining labels whose values sum to n. Leading quantifiers are universal over finite or countable arithmetic objects; finite representation witnesses are existential. The claim is not universal over sets of reals.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-representability property at the fixed stated reciprocal threshold, not an extremal numerical optimization or a density upper bound. An unspecified N(D,k,F) settles the claim.
shape.ambient_structure: Exact integer arithmetic and ordering coexist. Bases4,8,16 admit a shared binary exponent coordinate, with periodicity twelve and labelled multiplicities. Classical signed-weight interval criteria and finite unit groups modulo powers of two are known tools. Disjoint union and fresh-tail recursion are the proposed amplifications. No structured/random dichotomy, pairwise probabilistic overlap parameter or proved category transport is recorded.
shape.symmetries: Base ordering and relabelling do not affect legal sums. Base addition, lowering the cutoff and removing fewer labels preserve any represented set, subject to keeping the stated input hypotheses. Arbitrary translation or dilation need not preserve the labelled pure-power supplies. No density-increment system of invariant pieces is recorded.
shape.configuration: Every integer beyond an input-dependent threshold must be an exact positive sum of distinct remaining labels, with equal numerical values separately available. Proposed signed digits must split into disjoint positive alternatives, and successive gadgets must exclude both earlier supports. Restricting bases can remove4,8,16 or every odd base, destroying the digit alphabet, gcd or reciprocal reserve. Deduplicating equal values, arbitrary scaling or untracked truncation can destroy the required labelled configuration.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal construction or optimal threshold is asserted. The candidate is a finite interval made from bases4,8,16 and an odd b, with all other bases kept as a disjoint syndetic reserve.
shape.finite_certificates: For fixed D,k,F, an interval of the reserve gap length with a legal finite representation of every point is a positive finite certificate once the reserve lemma is proved. A single two-choice unit motif has positive gain one. The prospective finite signed block and exact label identities can be checked by hand or encoded for a solver, but no global finite reduction or mathematical run is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: Yes: adding bases, lowering a positive cutoff and deleting fewer labels enlarge the represented set when the stated input hypotheses remain valid. The smallest positive cutoff is one, but all positive cutoffs are required. Raising the fixed reciprocal threshold restricts the input family and gives a weaker assertion.
shape.uniformity_parameter: D, its size and base values, the positive cutoff k, finite deletion F and eventual integer n are unbounded. The threshold N may depend on D,k,F. No uniform N across inputs is required.
